projects.title: Improving Q&A System of CDA using Large Language Models
details: Researching different methods to improve Q&A system of the chatbot specifically using LLMs as both a retriever and a generator in the RAG pipeline.
At retriever stage, first doing course level retrieval using hybrid approach of embedding models and then fine-level retrieval using LLM to avoid context length saturation.
Using Attentive Reasoning Queries (ARQ) prompting technique to instruct both retriever and generator LLMs to effectively reduce attention drift.

projects.title: Guard-railing Generative AI using LLM-as-Judge Metrics and SLM finetuned Metrics
details: Explored metric creation using LLM as a Judge for rapid development and performance evaluation of RAG based Q&A system.
LORA finetuned Small Language Models around 7-15B parameter models to safeguard from sharing critically wrong/senstive answers in production.
Devised modified-PPO based RL training regime based on Reinforcement-Learning-through-Verifiable-Rewards (RLVR) to reduce accuracy gap between LLM and SLM performance.

industryExperience.organisation: Amazon AGI Speech Team (Previously Alexa ASR)

projects.title: Bootstrapping ASR for Rapid Language Expansion in a BOOM
details: Built ASR framework addressing challenges of building systems for new languages without large labelled data corpus.
Explored leveraging foundation models, distilling from massive multilingual teacher models for acountic encoder pre-training, and semi-supervised learning (SSL).
Used Text-to-Speech augmentation to boost model performance under extreme low resource scenarios.
Demonstrated effective amalgamation of training strategies enabling boot-strapping new languages with 10x less labelled data requirements and launch ready WER.
Setup data pipeline for open source multi-lingual data sources and proposed curriculum learning approach for scaling model on ever-increasing leanguage set.

thesis.title: Novel Neural Architectures Based on Recurrent Connections & Symmetric Filters for Visual Processing
description: Proposed two neural network architectures inspired from the neuronal pathways present in the human brain. First is a type of Recurrent Convolutional Neural Network layer called as Long-Short-Term-Convolutional-Neural-Network (LST_CNN) and the other is a Symmetric Convolutional Neural Network layer based on Symmetric Filters.

The proposed LST_CNN layer is not just limited to spatial learning but is also capable of exploiting temporal knowledge from the data due to the implicit presence of recurrence in the structure. Tested its capability on object detection and tracking.

Filter weights from deep SOTA networks when visualized show symmetric patterns. This is in strong correlation with the visual cortex in human brain which has evolved in detecting the pervasive symmetry present in nature. Exploiting this, the proposed symmetric convolutional layer reduces not only computational resources but also memory footprint without hampering the accuracy compared to the standard convolutional layer.

projects.projectTitle: RTOS Kit and Serial to USB(/SD card) Standalone Module
projects.shortInfo: Real time operating systems (RTOS) are used in environments where a large number of events, mostly external to the computer system, must be accepted and processed in a short time or within certain deadlines. Such applications are industrial control, telephone switching equipment, flight control, and real time simulations. Project main was to create RTOS kit for Electronics Department of WCE so that students can perform RTOS based practicals. Another part of the project was to create a hand sized standalone module which can accept serial data using RX/TX lines and process-convert them into USB/SD card data. This is specifically an important application as all controllers however big or small have serial input and ouput

In some situations it is impossible for humans to explore a certain terrain without risking life. Unmanned aerial vehicles (UAV) can provide a very simplified way to access such areas, giving useful visual aid to the rescue team. Even though being such a useful piece of technology it is very costly. Our aim was to build a drone with minimum cost and adequate features and implement the whole system.

Nyquist Sampling theroem is one of most important theorem in Digital Signal Processing field. In this project we wanted to see what happens to signal when it is sampled at different sampling rates. Main aim was to learn EDA tools and build our own hand-made PCB(Printed Circuit Board).

Developed a neural network trained end-to-end on both object detection and tracking. Built on YOLOv3 architecture to simultaneously learn spatila features from the images and temporal dependencies between features. Tested on Object Tracking Benchmark (OTB) dataset. The network not only learned to track the main annotated object but also generalized to multiple objects present in the video, inferring that tracking capability extends to all classes the detector can identify.

projects.projectTitle: Symmetric Convolutional Filters: A Novel Way to Constrain Parameters in CNN
projects.shortInfo: Created a new type of Convolutional Layer using Symmetrical filter weights to reduce memory footprint and computational resources of SOTA neural networks. Experiments showed significant memory reduction with minimal accuracy trade-off. When used only on first few layers, it even showed better accuracy than original SOTA networks. Research leveraged the inherent symmetric patterns found in deep network filter weights, correlating with visual cortex evolution for detecting pervasive symmetry in nature.

Competed in 'Clog Loss: Alzheimer's Research with Stall Catchers' hosted by MATHWORKS on DrivenData. Objective was to classify brain blood vessel segments as flowing or stalled. Created a two-stage neural network with Inception-v3 followed by LSTM cells, trained on 3D image stacks from live mouse brains. Achieved rank of 29 out of 923 participants, performing better than 96% of competitors.

Ideation project to develop technology for detecting slipper surfaces on roads using Remote Sensing concepts. Solution based on two key principles: (1) light of different wavelengths reflects differently based on surface roughness - specular reflection on smooth surfaces vs diffuse on rough surfaces, and (2) water's high absorption coefficient for Short Wave Infra-Red light makes wet surfaces appear dark relative to surrounding road surface, based on NASA Jet Propulsion Laboratory experiments.
